topic-008-convergence-and-recovery-guara.evolution: The early representatives compare self-organizing and information-based clustering. Work in the 2000s develops spectral kernels, maximum-margin objectives, and analyses of spectral limitations. Later examples add multiple nonredundant views, scalable manifold constraints, and robust variable clustering, showing increasing attention to alternative geometries and uncertainty rather than one universal partition.
openQuestions: How can users distinguish a stable cluster from an artifact of the similarity measure?
Which guarantees survive noisy or conflicting views of the same data?
topic-008-convergence-and-recovery-guara.overview: Clustering seeks useful groups without supplied labels, but the answer depends on the geometry and objective used to define similarity. These papers develop spectral, discriminative, manifold, and subspace approaches. Kernel eigenvectors, relaxed partition objectives, and robust regressions offer different ways to recover group structure beyond simple distance to a center.
topic-008-convergence-and-recovery-guara.title: Spectral and Subspace Clustering
topic-008-convergence-and-recovery-guara.whyItMatters: Real datasets can contain curved groups, multiple views, noise, or correlated variables. Understanding which structure a clustering method assumes is essential before treating its output as a meaningful organization of the data.

topic-009-4dbinfer-a-4d-benchmarking-too.evolution: Earlier work explores hierarchical relational embeddings and graph-based concepts. The 2019–2023 representatives focus on long-range dependencies, subgraph reasoning, and logical queries over unseen entities and relations. Recent database work asks which graph representation actually supports the downstream task, balancing removal of irrelevant structure against addition of useful connections.
openQuestions: Which relational patterns transfer when both entity types and relation vocabularies change?
How can graph optimization preserve semantics while simplifying computation?
topic-009-4dbinfer-a-4d-benchmarking-too.overview: Relational learning predicts links and answers queries using the pattern of connections among entities. This topic emphasizes generalization to new entities, relations, or databases rather than memorizing one fixed graph. Relation graphs, structural representations, and learned graph construction help models reuse relational patterns across changing data.
topic-009-4dbinfer-a-4d-benchmarking-too.title: Inductive Learning on Relational Graphs
topic-009-4dbinfer-a-4d-benchmarking-too.whyItMatters: A knowledge base or database evolves after training. Systems that depend on a separate learned embedding for every known entity can struggle when new objects arrive, making inductive structure essential for reusable reasoning.

topic-010-3d-aware-scene-manipulation-vi.evolution: The collection begins with probabilistic image-generation and interpretation models. Later examples combine attention and style modulation to organize scenes and geometric variation. Recent work expands into multimodal flow-based synthesis and detector-guided exploration of generative space, reflecting complementary interests in producing images and understanding their distinctive failure modes.
openQuestions: How can generators preserve object relationships while allowing local edits?
Which generated variations are missing from standard sampling-based evaluations?
topic-010-3d-aware-scene-manipulation-vi.overview: Visual generators must represent objects, geometry, and long-range scene relationships while producing convincing pixels. The central representatives study compositional latent variables, spatially modulated generators, inverse graphics, and score-based synthesis. Related detection work examines the space of generated images to understand where synthetic-image classifiers fail.
topic-010-3d-aware-scene-manipulation-vi.title: Structured Visual Generation and Synthetic-Image Analysis
topic-010-3d-aware-scene-manipulation-vi.whyItMatters: Good visual quality alone does not guarantee controllable geometry or broad coverage of possible outputs. Structured generation can make synthesis easier to interpret and manipulate, while systematic exploration of that structure can improve evaluation and detection.

topic-011-a-computational-decision-theor.evolution: Early representatives address incremental planning and learning without explicit state estimation. Later work introduces Bayesian adaptation and online planning guarantees. The 2024–2026 evidence develops provable representations, finite-history reductions with quantified approximation error, and geometric descriptions that expose optimization difficulties unique to partial observability.
openQuestions: How much history is necessary when the environment changes?
Can practical belief approximations provide reliable error estimates for the resulting policy?
topic-011-a-computational-decision-theor.overview: When an agent cannot directly observe the state, its decisions must depend on beliefs or informative histories rather than the latest observation alone. These papers study POMDP representations, planning algorithms, policy optimization, and the geometry of achievable value functions. Approximation is central because exact belief-space reasoning can be computationally and statistically difficult.
topic-011-a-computational-decision-theor.title: Planning and Learning under Partial Observability
topic-011-a-computational-decision-theor.whyItMatters: Treating an observation as a complete state can produce systematically poor actions. Useful approximations need to preserve enough history for decision-making while making learning and planning feasible.

topic-012-quest-query-aware-sparsity-for.evolution: Early representatives investigate cache-based language models, memory access, and parallel decoding. The 2024–2025 work targets bandwidth and token selection. Recent methods learn eviction policies, preserve evicted content in latent memory, and exploit shared low-rank structure across layers, extending the design space beyond simply keeping fewer tokens.
openQuestions: How can a model recognize that an evicted detail has become important?
Which memory tests predict failure in realistic multi-turn workloads?
topic-012-quest-query-aware-sparsity-for.overview: Long-context language models must retain useful past information without letting attention memory dominate inference cost. This cluster studies key-value cache compression, eviction, recomputation, sparse attention, and recurrent summaries. Methods differ in whether discarded information can be recovered and whether importance is estimated for the current query or learned across contexts.
topic-012-quest-query-aware-sparsity-for.title: Long-Context Memory and KV-Cache Efficiency
topic-012-quest-query-aware-sparsity-for.whyItMatters: A bounded cache can speed decoding yet silently erase information needed much later. Efficiency therefore has to be assessed alongside long-range retrieval, multi-turn consistency, and sensitivity to aggressive compression.

topic-013-nabla-2-dft-a-universal-quantu.evolution: Early examples study constrained atomic representations and reaction prediction. Later work develops invariant molecular features, equivariant wavefunction prediction, and conformation generation. Recent representatives scrutinize scaling tradeoffs, align generators with learned force fields, and benchmark neural-wavefunction expressivity across different quantum regimes.
openQuestions: When should symmetry be imposed architecturally rather than learned from data?
How can benchmarks reveal failures outside the chemical or quantum regimes used for training?
topic-013-nabla-2-dft-a-universal-quantu.overview: Machine learning can approximate energies, forces, wavefunctions, and molecular structures that are expensive to obtain through physical calculations. This topic examines representations that respect or learn geometric transformations, as well as architectures and benchmarks for scaling atomistic prediction. It connects molecular generation with the more detailed electronic descriptions used to derive physical observables.
topic-013-nabla-2-dft-a-universal-quantu.title: Molecular Geometry and Neural Quantum Models
topic-013-nabla-2-dft-a-universal-quantu.whyItMatters: Fast surrogates can expand the range of systems and candidate molecules researchers explore. Their usefulness depends on physical accuracy, transfer across chemical domains, and computational cost, not only performance on familiar configurations.

topic-014-text-g-2-text-m-a-generalized-.evolution: The earliest representatives develop practical and non-greedy selection strategies. Later methods exploit manifold or kernel structure and dependencies among features. More recent work emphasizes generalization guarantees, bagging-based stability, and source screening, including cases where discarding seemingly relevant data improves shared-subspace estimation.
openQuestions: How should selection report uncertainty when several correlated subsets work equally well?
Can stability be improved without hiding genuinely heterogeneous signals?
topic-014-text-g-2-text-m-a-generalized-.overview: Feature selection identifies which measured variables are sufficient for useful prediction or representation. The cluster includes kernel-space selection, unsupervised scoring, redundancy-aware methods, and stability analysis. Related work asks which data sources best support a shared representation, extending selection from coordinates to the evidence used to learn them.
topic-014-text-g-2-text-m-a-generalized-.title: Feature Selection, Stability, and Informative Subsets
topic-014-text-g-2-text-m-a-generalized-.whyItMatters: Reducing inputs can lower acquisition cost and improve interpretability, but unstable selections can give misleading scientific conclusions. A small subset should retain useful information and remain reasonably consistent under changes in the sample.

topic-015-texttt-strcmp-integrating-grap.evolution: Early representatives compare soft assignment and genetic-search strategies, followed by learning to guide branch-and-bound. Recent work learns distributions of candidate solutions, adapts policies in latent spaces, and selects among solvers. The 2026 evidence distinguishes proposing promising actions from committing to one, motivating more transferable proposal-and-selection designs.
openQuestions: Which learned search components generalize across problem families and scales?
How can solution-quality guarantees be retained during rapid online adaptation?
topic-015-texttt-strcmp-integrating-grap.overview: Combinatorial problems require choosing discrete structures from an enormous candidate space. These papers use learned policies, continuous proposal spaces, meta-learning, and memory to guide search for routing and other optimization tasks. The dominant theme is learning where to search or how to adapt a solver, rather than replacing feasibility constraints with an unconstrained prediction.
topic-015-texttt-strcmp-integrating-grap.title: Learning-Guided Combinatorial Search
topic-015-texttt-strcmp-integrating-grap.whyItMatters: A neural solver that works only on its training distribution may fail when instance size or structure changes. Combining learned proposals with adaptable selection and explicit search can improve both scalability and robustness.
